summary: Lair Mountain tower in Tolland: a 1934 60-foot CCC-built Aermotor, sold on eBay in 2003; a 2005 survey found only footings remain.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor tower built in 1934 by CCC crews from camp 64 in Chester, with ECW funds (FFLOS)
facts.status_note: Sold on eBay in 2003; a 2005 survey by New England FFLA members found only footings remain (FFLOS).

events.note: FFLOS dates the first 40-foot Aermotor to 1915 and calls it the former Becket Mountain tower; other accounts give 1913 or 1914
Tower moved from Becket Mountain to Lair's Hill and given a 20-foot extension (1916 state report; Becket history). 1915 rebuild on Lair also reported
New 60-foot Aermotor built by CCC boys from camp 64 in Chester with ECW funds
New road and power line added
Survey by New England FFLA members confirmed only footings remain

evidence.supports: First tower built in 1915 as a 40-foot Aermotor
evidence.quote: The first tower, a 40' Aermotor with 8'x8' cab, was built in 1915.

evidence.supports: That first tower was the former Becket Mountain tower
evidence.quote: That tower was the former Becket Mountain tower in Becket.

evidence.supports: 1934 60-foot Aermotor built by CCC crews from camp 64 with ECW funds
evidence.quote: In 1934, a new 60' Aermotor tower was built by the the CCC boys from camp 64 in Chester with ECW funds.

evidence.supports: Road and power line added in 1958
evidence.quote: In 1958, a new road and a power line were added.
This tower was sold on eBay in 2003.
A 2005 survey by New England FFLA Members confirmed that only footings remain of this tower.

evidence.supports: 1916 Annual Report of the State Forester, quoted on Forest Lookouts: 30-foot tower moved from Becket to Lair's Hill with 20-foot extension
evidence.quote: A 30-foot tower which has been in use for the past three years on Becket Mountain in the town of Becket has been taken down and removed to Lair's Hill in Tolland, where an extension of 20 feet was added.

evidence.supports: Becket history gives the move as 1916
evidence.quote: In 1916, the tower was moved from Becket Mountain to Lair Mountain in Tolland, where an extension of 20 feet was added.

evidence.supports: Becket history gives the original build as 1913
evidence.quote: In 1913, a 30-foot steel tower was built (maybe 40 feet).
Another sources says it was built in 1914, and closed permanently at the end of the season.

evidence.supports: Rebuilt on Lair Mountain in 1915 per the alternative account
evidence.quote: stored until 1915, when it was rebuilt on Lair Mountain in Tolland

corrections.why: FFLOS describes the tower sold in 2003 as the 60-foot 1934 Aermotor. 9.1 m (30 ft) matches the earlier 30-foot Becket tower before its 20-foot extension at Lair.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS dates the first tower to 1915. The 1916 state report (quoted on Forest Lookouts) implies a tower used for three years before the 1916 move. The Becket history gives 1913 for the build, 1914 in an alternative account, and 1916 for the move. The story gives the range and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: FFLA Massachusetts Facebook posts (not fetchable, search snippets only) describe the Lair tower as an Aermotor MC-39 that was dismantled in late 2004. That differs from the 2003 eBay sale in the FFLOS record, so it is not cited. The Tolland State Forest map PDF returned no text. No source read covers current public access to Lair Mountain. The 1916 extension makes 50 ft; the 9.1 m height in the brief is the pre-extension 30 ft.
